text: P samples i.i.d. losses at each perturbed decision and forms empirical CVaR from the whole batch (P lines 409-459); its finite-sample term comes from a DKW CDF bound, \(\mathbb E|\widehat C^i-C^i|\le d^0U_i\sqrt{2\pi}/(\alpha_i\sqrt{s_k^i})\) before multiplying by \(d/\delta_i\) (P lines 1289-1325). A predicted VaR alone does not change the query distribution or create additional tail observations, so the scan hypothesis needs a specified stronger oracle or a different estimator before a query reduction claim is meaningful. Q itself says prediction cost and error-to-downstream-cost reductions require explicit models (Q lines 944-959, 973-979). I am checking for a sharper theorem or a genuine obstacle.

Initial scan hypothesis is weak under P's stated oracle: each query returns a full noisy loss \(J^i(x,\xi)\), and empirical CVaR minimizes over \(\tau\) after \(s_k^i\) iid losses are acquired (P lines 418–445). Seeding the quantile only speeds the scalar minimization, not the \(s_k^i\) loss queries or the DKW \(s^{-1/2}\) term (P lines 1299–1324). I am testing a different construction: retain the Rockafellar–Uryasev threshold as a jointly optimized state, using a single sampled hinge per update; this could remove finite-batch CVaR bias and make a predictor a warm start for \(\tau\). Q's prediction-cost and interface cautions at lines 159–161, 342, 401–405 apply.

Candidate theorem: optimize the lifted objective \(F_i(x,\tau_i)=\tau_i+\alpha_i^{-1}\mathbb E[(J^i(x,\xi)-\tau_i)_+]\) jointly over shared \(x\) and local \(\tau_i\in[-U_i,U_i]\). P already states this representation (lines 327–338), and samplewise convexity/boundedness (lines 495–501). One fresh loss gives \(h_i=\tau_i+\alpha_i^{-1}(J^i(y_i+\delta_i u_i,\xi)-\tau_i)_+\), \(g_x=(d/\delta_i)h_i u_i\), \(g_{\tau}=1-\alpha_i^{-1}\mathbf1\{J^i>\tau_i\}\) (choose a valid subgradient at equality). Conditional expectations are a gradient in \(x\) and subgradient in \(\tau_i\) of the fixed smoothed lifted objective. Thus no empirical-CVaR/DKW bias occurs, while variance scales as \(O(d^2U_i^2/(\alpha_i^2\delta_i^2))\) and smoothing bias as \(O(L_i\delta_i/\alpha_i)\). A predicted quantile can initialize clipped \(\tau_i\); its error enters only the initial-distance term and arbitrary predictions retain a bounded term. This is a plausible one-query-per-agent-per-step variant, but the benefit from accurate prediction may be only a constant, not better query-complexity order.

Sharper candidate: predict the local CVaR value \(b_k^i\approx C^i(y_k^i)\) at the unperturbed point, clip it to \([-U_i,U_i]\), and use \(\widetilde g_k^i=(d/\delta_i)(\widehat C_k^i(y_k^i+\delta_i u_k^i)-b_k^i)u_k^i\). If \(b_k^i\) is fixed before the current direction, \(\mathbb E[b_k^i u_k^i\mid\mathcal F_k]=0\), so the gradient bias and P recursion are unchanged. Since \(C^i\) is \(L_i\)-Lipschitz (P lines 505-507), conditional second moment is at most \(3d^2[L_i^2+|b_k^i-C^i(y_k^i)|^2/\delta_i^2+4U_i^2/(\alpha_i^2s_k^i\delta_i^2)]\) via the DKW proof (P lines 1289-1325). Clipping gives a prediction-independent bound of the same order as P's \(d^2U_i^2/\delta_i^2\); accurate predictions remove that baseline variance. This targets the \(G_{\max}^2\sum\eta_k^2/\sum\eta_k\) term in P's ergodic theorem (lines 657-670). Still checking whether it yields actual oracle complexity gains after CVaR sampling bias.

Cross-check and strengthening of ada's lifted-state idea (#3): the \(x\)-gradient should subtract the known direction-independent \(\tau_i\): \(g_x=(d/(\alpha_i\delta_i))(J^i(y_i+\delta_i u_i,\xi)-\tau_i)_+u_i\). This is still unbiased for the smoothed lifted objective because \(\mathbb E[u_i]=0\), but when \(\tau_i\) is an accurate VaR at queried points, \(\Pr\{J^i>\tau_i\}\approx\alpha_i\) and the conditional second moment improves from \(O(d^2U_i^2/(\alpha_i^2\delta_i^2))\) to \(O(d^2U_i^2/(\alpha_i\delta_i^2))\). For any clipped \(\tau_i\), the original \(\alpha_i^{-2}\) worst-case cap remains. A predictor of VaR at the center can control tail probability at perturbed points if one assumes a local anti-concentration/quantile stability condition; alternatively define prediction error directly as excess-tail probability \(p_i-\alpha_i\). This may turn the quantile into a meaningful variance control, whereas mere initialization changes only the first distance term.

Prior-work check limits novelty: Soma & Yoshida, "Statistical Learning with Conditional Value at Risk" (2020), https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.05826, already optimize CVaR jointly in decision and threshold using one iid sample per stochastic first-order step. Wang, Shen & Zavlanos (ICML 2022), https://proceedings.mlr.press/v162/wang22w.html, use one-point zeroth-order CVaR estimates with sampled losses in games. Thus the lifted one-query construction is an adaptation to P's time-varying distributed zeroth-order setting, not a new CVaR trick. Queried: "zeroth order CVaR optimization joint VaR threshold stochastic gradient one sample paper"; "distributed decentralized CVaR stochastic optimization VaR auxiliary variable zeroth order"; "bandit CVaR threshold convex optimization". I found no direct identical theorem in these searches, which is not a novelty claim.

Model caution: Q defines consistency/robustness as cost ratios against an offline \(\mathrm{OPT}>0\) (Q lines 257-343), whereas P proves an additive expected CVaR optimality gap for a stochastic convex objective (P lines 657-670). Any combined theorem should explicitly use an additive error-sensitive gap, not import Q's ratio language verbatim. The lifted estimator in #3, with the \(\tau_i\) baseline subtraction in #5, offers a clean per-iterate variance term \(\mathbb E\|g_{x,k}^i\|^2\le 4d^2U_i^2 p_k^i/(\alpha_i^2\delta_i^2)\), where \(p_k^i=\Pr\{J^i(y_k^i+\delta_i u_k^i,\xi)>\tau_k^i\mid\mathcal F_k\}\) averages over the current direction. At a correct upper-tail quantile \(p_k^i\le\alpha_i\), improving the term by \(1/\alpha_i\); arbitrary advice has \(p_k^i\le1\). This is a conditional, testable prediction-error measure, but maintaining \(p_k^i\approx\alpha_i\) across changing decisions needs analysis.

Possible main result, sharpened from the scan: jointly optimize P's \(F_i(x,\tau_i)=\tau_i+\alpha_i^{-1}\mathbb E(J_i(x,\xi)-\tau_i)_+\) using one loss/agent/round and direction-independent threshold subtraction in the \(x\)-estimator. Standard projected distributed stochastic-approximation algebra should yield an additive ergodic gap of the form \(\frac{D_x^2+4m^{-1}\sum_iU_i^2}{2\sum_k\eta_k}+\frac{\sum_k\eta_k^2\sum_i[4d^2U_i^2p_{ik}/(\alpha_i^2\delta_i^2)+O(1/\alpha_i^2)]}{2m\sum_k\eta_k}+\text{network disagreement}+O(\max_iL_i\delta_i/\alpha_i)\), with no P-style \(1/(\alpha_i\delta_i\sqrt{s_i})\) floor. Correct-quantile tail probabilities \(p_{ik}\le\alpha_i\) improve the stochastic term by an \(\alpha_i\) factor, while \(p_{ik}\le1\) gives a uniform cap. This changes the question from 'seed empirical CVaR sampling' to 'can quantile advice control tail-activation variance in one-query distributed zeroth-order CVaR optimization?' Caveat: the stochastic threshold iterates must stay calibrated as \(x\) moves, and the \(O(L_i\delta_i/\alpha_i)\) smoothing penalty may dominate unless carefully optimized. Existing joint-threshold first-order CVaR work noted by ada (#6) limits novelty.

Limit on the original query-saving story: even an exact VaR cannot identify the tail mean from free information. At a fixed \(x\), take \(J=0\) with probability \(1-\alpha\), and conditional on the \(\alpha\)-tail let \(J\in\{U/2,U\}\) with probabilities \(1/2\mp\theta,1/2\pm\theta\). In both models the upper-tail VaR can be \(0\), but CVaR differs by \(U\theta\), while each ordinary loss query distinguishes the models only with probability \(\alpha\). Standard two-point testing then needs \(\Omega(U^2/(\alpha\varepsilon^2))\) iid loss queries to estimate CVaR to error \(\varepsilon\). This is a derivation from the oracle model, not a literature novelty claim. It supports replacing the scan's 'quantile seeds samples' premise with variance-aware optimization and keeping an unavoidable rare-tail cost.

Prior-work correction to my #4: Wang, Shen, and Zavlanos (ICML 2022) explicitly analyze residual feedback using previous CVaR estimates to reduce variance of one-point CVaR gradients: https://proceedings.mlr.press/v162/wang22w.html (abstract lines 14-17). Thus a predicted CVaR scalar baseline is a clean error-sensitive extension of an existing variance-reduction idea, not a wholly new mechanism. It may be less publication-worthy than the joint-threshold, single-sample construction plus quantified tail-activation variance. My search queries were '"zeroth-order" "CVaR" "threshold" "distributed" optimization' and '"CVaR" "one-point" "baseline" variance quantile zeroth order'; no exact same theorem surfaced, but this is not evidence of novelty.

Cross-check of emmy #5: correct. With one fresh loss and a local threshold, use \(g_x^i=d(\,J^i(y_i+\delta_i u_i,\xi)-t_i\,)_+u_i/(\alpha_i\delta_i)\), \(g_t^i=1-\mathbf1\{J^i>t_i\}/\alpha_i\). Writing \(p_{i,k}=\Pr\{J^i(y_i+\delta_i u_i,\xi)>t_i\mid\mathcal F_k\}\), conditional second moments are bounded by \(4d^2U_i^2p_{i,k}/(\alpha_i^2\delta_i^2)\) and \(1-2p_{i,k}/\alpha_i+p_{i,k}/\alpha_i^2\). Thus \(p=O(\alpha_i)\) yields \(1/\alpha_i\) rather than \(1/\alpha_i^2\) variance dependence, while \(p\le1\) is a robust cap. Samplewise Lipschitz losses plus a density bound \(M_i\) on the crossed interval yield \(p_{i,k}\le\alpha_i+M_i(|t_i-q_i(y_i)|+L_i\delta_i)\). But one-shot quantile accuracy does not ensure this holds along the iterates; a predictor interface or tracking theorem is needed. Full derivation and source pointers: ada/quantile_lift_note.md. Style gates passed.

Important improvement/correction to #8 and ada's note: the lifted objective has a pointwise-in-\(t\) smoothing bound \(|F_{i,\delta}(x,t)-F_i(x,t)|\le L_i\delta_i/\alpha_i\), but the *optimized* lifted objective has the sharper \(\alpha_i\)-free bound. Indeed \(F_{i,\delta}(x,t)\) is the RU representation of CVaR of \(J_i(x+\delta_i\nu,\xi)\) over joint \((\nu,\xi)\); samplewise Lipschitzness couples this loss to \(J_i(x,\xi)\) within \(L_i\delta_i\) almost surely. CVaR monotonicity and translation invariance then give \(|\min_tF_{i,\delta}(x,t)-C_i(x)|\le L_i\delta_i\). For any threshold iterate \(t\), \(F_{i,\delta}(x,t)\ge C_i(x)-L_i\delta_i\); for a comparator choose the smoothed optimal \(t^*_{i,\delta}(x^*)\), giving \(F_{i,\delta}(x^*,t^*)\le C_i(x^*)+L_i\delta_i\). Thus the distributed true-CVaR gap can pay \(O(L_i\delta_i)\), not \(O(L_i\delta_i/\alpha_i)\), plus P's domain-shrink term. This changes indicative homogeneous query scaling from \(\alpha^{-4}\varepsilon^{-4}\) to \(\alpha^{-2}\varepsilon^{-4}\) in the worst case, or \(\alpha^{-1}\varepsilon^{-4}\) if tail activation remains \(O(\alpha)\), against P's displayed bound requiring roughly \(\alpha^{-2}\varepsilon^{-8}\) queries for small \(\varepsilon\) (ignoring constants/network). These are comparisons of displayed upper bounds, not minimax claims.

I completed a single-agent finite-time proposition in ada/quantile_lift_note.md. With comparator \((z_\delta,t^\star)\), \(z_\delta=(1-\delta/r)x^\star\), the additive expected CVaR gap of the step-size-weighted average is bounded by \((\|x_0-z_\delta\|^2+|t_0-t^\star|^2)/(2H_T)\), plus \((2H_T)^{-1}\sum_{k<T}\eta_k^2\mathbb E[4d^2U^2p_k/(\alpha^2\delta^2)+1-2p_k/\alpha+p_k/\alpha^2]\), plus \(L\delta(2+\|x^\star\|/r)/\alpha\). This follows directly from joint convexity, one-point smoothing, projected stochastic-subgradient recursion, and P's shrunken-domain comparator. It is a precise additive consistency/robustness statement for *initialization* (perfect quantile zeroes one distance term; clipping caps it at \(4U^2\)). A full distributed theorem and a maintained-calibration theorem remain unproved; Q's ratio definitions cannot be transferred literally, as emmy #7 notes. Style gates passed.

Refinement to #12 and ada #13: for the shrunken feasible set, compare against \((z_\delta,t^*_{\delta}(z_\delta))\), where \(z_\delta=(1-\delta/r)x^*\) and \(t^*_{\delta}(z_\delta)\in\arg\min_t F_\delta(z_\delta,t)\). Then \(\min_tF_\delta(z_\delta,t)\le C(z_\delta)+L\delta\le C(x^*)+L\delta+LD_x\delta/r\); and \(F_\delta(x,t)\ge C(x)-L\delta\). This yields \(L\delta(2+D_x/r)\) smoothing/shrink cost in the single-agent gap, with *no* \(1/\alpha\), while changing only the comparator threshold in the initial-distance term. If one instead fixes \(t^*\) at \(x^*\) and moves \(x\) to \(z_\delta\), the crude \(L\delta/\alpha\) Lipschitz bound returns. This is a genuine tightening of the theorem, not just notation.

Remaining prediction-interface obstacle to #13: if 'perfect quantile prediction' means the VaR at the observable initial decision \(x_0\), it need not equal the comparator threshold \(t^*_{\delta}(z_\delta)\) at the unknown optimal/shrunken decision. Hence its exactness does not generally zero the initialization term. One could define advice as a prediction of that comparator threshold, but Q's interface (Q lines 257-263) requires specifying what observable context makes this a legitimate pre-run target. Similarly, a sequence of predicted VaRs at current \(y_k\) can be evaluated after \(y_k\) is known, but using it to reset \(t_k\) needs a new regret/tracking proof. The one-query lifted theorem is credible without advice; the learning-augmented speedup remains conditional on a causal calibration mechanism.

Current synthesis: The scan's predicted-VaR seeding claim fails under P's actual iid full-loss oracle: quantile advice does not by itself reduce the empirical-CVaR batch (P lines 404-445, 1289-1325). The most concrete route is the one-query lifted method (ada #3, #13; P's RU representation lines 327-338), with the threshold-subtracted hinge gradient (#5/#11), a robust second-moment cap \(p_k\le1\), and a variance gain when thresholds are calibrated so \(p_k=O(\alpha)\). My #12/#14 tighten the smoothing/shrink term to \(L\delta(2+D_x/r)\), independent of \(\alpha\), by comparing to the smoothed optimal threshold at the shrunken comparator; thus the indicative single-agent iid-query upper bound is \(O(\alpha^{-2}\varepsilon^{-4})\) worst case and \(O(\alpha^{-1}\varepsilon^{-4})\) if calibrated tail occupancy persists, versus \(O(\alpha^{-2}\varepsilon^{-8})\) from P's displayed bound under homogeneous tuning, ignoring constants/network. This is a promising theorem project, not a demonstrated publication result. First-order joint-threshold CVaR SGD already exists (https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.05826); one-point CVaR residual feedback already exists (https://proceedings.mlr.press/v162/wang22w.html). The specific value would be distributed time-varying-network one-query analysis plus a causal, error-sensitive quantile mechanism, measured with additive CVaR gap rather than Q's competitive ratios (Q lines 257-343). Unresolved: prove the full network recursion, show advice observed at current decisions can keep thresholds calibrated without breaking the stochastic approximation proof, compare under matched query budgets, and check broader prior work. If that advice mechanism cannot be proved, the pair's Q-specific novelty is weak despite the lifted method's improvement over P's displayed analysis.

Correction to my #13 after emmy #12: the \(\alpha^{-1}\) smoothing term is unnecessarily loose for the *optimized* lifted objective. For each \(x\), \(\min_tF_\delta(x,t)\) is CVaR of \(J(x+\delta\nu,\xi)\), and the coupling \(|J(x+\delta\nu,\xi)-J(x,\xi)|\le L\delta\) gives \(|\min_tF_\delta(x,t)-C(x)|\le L\delta\). Choosing comparator \(t_\delta^\star\in\arg\min_tF_\delta(z_\delta,t)\) yields the same finite-time bound as #13 but with \(L\delta(2+\|x^\star\|/r)\) rather than \(L\delta(2+\|x^\star\|/r)/\alpha\). The initial prediction error is now measured against the *smoothed quantile at \(z_\delta\)*, not necessarily the VaR at \(x^\star\); connecting those targets requires quantile stability. Revised ada/quantile_lift_note.md and reran both style gates successfully.
ready at #17

A small rate-accounting correction to emmy #16: P's *displayed* polynomial-step finite-horizon order (P lines 752–775) is \(\rho_{1/2}(T)/\delta^2+\delta+e_s/(\alpha\delta)\), with \(\rho_{1/2}(T)=\log T/\sqrt T\). Homogeneous tuning for gap \(\varepsilon\) therefore needs \(\delta=O(\varepsilon)\), \(s=\Omega(\alpha^{-2}\varepsilon^{-4})\), and \(T=\widetilde\Omega(\varepsilon^{-6})\), giving \(\widetilde O(\alpha^{-2}\varepsilon^{-10})\) queries under that *displayed* guarantee. The \(\alpha^{-2}\varepsilon^{-8}\) comparison comes from reoptimizing P's step size in its underlying theorem, which is plausible but is not the displayed corollary. None of these upper-bound comparisons establishes a lower bound or publication novelty.

Current intention and conclusion: I changed the scan's question. The proposed VaR seed does not save queries for P's empirical-CVaR estimator under its full-loss iid oracle. The strongest supported line is a one-query lifted distributed zeroth-order CVaR method using a local threshold state, with threshold-subtracted hinge estimator and an additive gap bound driven by tail-activation probabilities \(p_{i,k}\); the single-agent theorem is worked out in ada/quantile_lift_note.md. Quantile advice can reduce the variance term by a factor of order \(\alpha_i\) only if calibration \(p_{i,k}=O(\alpha_i)\) persists, while \(p_{i,k}\le1\) gives robustness. This is a promising but unproved publication project, not an established result. The Q-specific gap is a causal prediction interface and a theorem maintaining calibration as \(x\) moves. Also unresolved: complete network proof, matched oracle-budget experiments, and broader prior-work check. I agree with emmy's interface objection #15; no claim that perfect advice at observable \(x_0\) equals the comparator quantile. I disagree only with the phrase 'P's displayed bound gives \(\varepsilon^{-8}\)' in #16; see rate correction #19.
ready at #20

I accept ada #19 and correct my #12/#16 comparison. P\(\!\)\(\text{\rm s}\) displayed polynomial-step corollary (P lines 752-775) has \(\rho_{1/2}(T)=\log T/\sqrt T\), so setting \(\delta=\Theta(\varepsilon)\), \(s=\Omega(\alpha^{-2}\varepsilon^{-4})\), and requiring \(\rho_{1/2}(T)/\delta^2=O(\varepsilon)\) gives \(T=\widetilde\Omega(\varepsilon^{-6})\), hence \(Ts=\widetilde O(\alpha^{-2}\varepsilon^{-10})\) as a sufficient upper-bound query budget (with the usual constants and feasibility caveats). My \(\alpha^{-2}\varepsilon^{-8}\) figure comes only from reoptimizing the constant step size in P\(\!\)\(\text{\rm s}\) underlying ergodic theorem (P lines 657-670), which gives \(T=O(\varepsilon^{-4})\) under homogeneous bounded-gradient scaling; it is not the displayed corollary. The lifted single-agent one-query estimate is \(O(\alpha^{-2}\varepsilon^{-4})\) in worst-case tail occupancy, or \(O(\alpha^{-1}\varepsilon^{-4})\) conditional on maintained \(p_k=O(\alpha)\), after tuning step size and \(\delta=O(\varepsilon)\). These compare sufficient upper bounds, not matched algorithms or lower bounds. The distributed theorem and causal calibration proof remain open.

A further publication test for the advice claim: the condition \(p_{i,k}=O(\alpha_i)\) is sufficient for the hinge-gradient variance gain but is not by itself evidence that predictions caused it. Starting every threshold at the known loss upper bound \(t_0^i=U_i\) also gives \(p_{i,0}=0\), and the threshold subgradient then drives it downward. A no-advice lifted algorithm might achieve similar trajectory-average tail occupancy under distributional regularity. Conversely, \(p\ll\alpha\) can simply mean an overlarge threshold, with low \(x\)-gradient variance but poor instantaneous objective. The additive regret bound remains valid because threshold error is paid elsewhere. For a Q-specific paper, compare to the best causal no-advice threshold rule and use an error measure tied to quantile distance or excess lifted objective, not just small \(p\). This is an objection to the claimed advice benefit, not to the one-query lifted theorem.
ready at #23

Additional distributed caveat after #22: the single-agent lifted rate cannot simply be copied to the network theorem. P bounds network disagreement through local-objective Lipschitzness (P lines 621–629, 657–670). At a fixed local threshold, \(F_{i,\delta}(x,t)=t+\alpha_i^{-1}\mathbb E(J^i(x+\delta\nu,\xi)-t)_+\) is at most \(L_i/\alpha_i\)-Lipschitz in \(x\), although the optimized CVaR is \(L_i\)-Lipschitz (P lines 505–507). Since the distributed recursion carries varying \(t_k^i\), its disagreement term may introduce additional \(\alpha_i^{-1}\) dependence. I added this qualification to ada/quantile_lift_note.md; both Markdown style gates pass. I accept emmy #22 rate correction as a comparison of sufficient upper bounds only.

I agree with emmy #23. Tail occupancy \(p_{i,k}=O(\alpha_i)\) is a variance condition, not a predictor-value certificate: the no-advice choice \(t_0^i=U_i\) has \(p_{i,0}=0\), and an overlarge threshold can lower \(p\) while worsening \(F_i(x,t)-C_i(x)\). A Q-specific result must use a causal quantile-error or excess-lifted-objective condition and beat a matched no-advice threshold trajectory, accounting for predictor cost. I added this caveat to ada/quantile_lift_note.md and reran both style gates. Thus the one-query lift stands as the supported algorithmic line; prediction-dependent query improvement is still unproved.
